explanation: Age rule incomplete. Observed SQL: year(2026-09-25) - year(birth) = 25 AND birthday (MMDD) <= 0925. It keeps only customers born in 2001 whose birthday has passed and drops those born in 2000 whose birthday falls after 25 Sept (year difference 26, completed age 25). Check: revenue of the dropped group = 268980 = 590320 - 321340.

Age rule over-constrained. Observed SQL: the first condition computes the completed age at order time correctly, but a second condition adds year(order) - 25 = year(birth) (its OR clause is always true), which removes orders placed before the 26th birthday by customers with a year difference of 26. Check: revenue of the removed orders = 439570 = 558980 - 119410.

Wrong age rule: birthday on the reference day instead of completed age. Observed SQL: birth year + 25 = 2026 AND birth month-day = 12-01, i.e. only customers born exactly on 2001-12-01. No customer has that birth date, hence 0 instead of 446690.

Contradictory filter. Observed SQL: (year difference 25 AND birthday passed) AND (year difference 25 AND birthday not passed AND year difference - 1 = 25). Both groups cannot hold at once (birthday passed and not passed; difference 25 and 26), so no row matches and COALESCE returns 0.

Same age error as C02. Observed SQL: year difference = 25 AND birthday passed on 2026-09-25; customers born in 2000 with a birthday after 25 Sept (completed age 25) are missing. Check: revenue of products a, b, c for the missing group = 165480 = 376740 - 211260.

Invalid SQL, not a wrong value. Observed: CAST((strftime('%Y', '2026-09-25') AS INTEGER) - CAST(...)) puts AS inside an extra parenthesis, which SQLite rejects (syntax error near "AS"); the sandbox returns no value. Hypothesis: with the parenthesis fixed, the age rule would still repeat the C02 error (year difference 25 only) and give 152730 instead of 258180.

Wrong age rule: order on the exact 25th birthday. Observed SQL: date(order) = birth_date + 25 years, i.e. only orders placed on the customer's 25th birthday instead of every order placed while aged 25. Check: those orders total 25290, the value returned.

Wrong age rule: birth date exactly 25 years before the reference date. Observed SQL: birth_date as YYYYMMDD = 20260925 - 250000, i.e. only customers born on 2001-09-25. One customer has that birth date but no product d order in Sept 2026, hence 0 instead of 1990.
